title: Senior Product Engineer, Education
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude Academy is where millions of people learn to use Claude and build fluency with AI. Our team built and launched it in-house. Now we're working out what learning looks like when AI is not just the subject of the lesson, but how we deliver learning. We're a small team of engineers, technical writers and designers, and we work closely with the educators who create the courses. We're hiring a product-minded software engineer to own large parts of Academy end-to-end, from the lesson a learner opens to the tools that get it published. Most of the hard problems here are ambiguous. You'll decide what's worth building, bring other teams along, and see it through to something people use. You can read more about how we approach teaching and learning AI . Responsibilities Own projects end to end: scope with stakeholders, design, build, ship, measure and operate, including security and privacy review Decide what to build by talking to learners, admins and experts, instrumenting what you ship, and stopping what doesn't work Build across the stack, from React and TypeScript front ends to the Go services behind them Build learning experiences powered by Claude, along with the evals that show whether they served the learner Drive work that crosses team lines, with product, security, privacy, infrastructure and go-to-market partners Raise the quality of the team's work through design docs, code review and mentoring Where you might focus Everyone works across Academy. Depending on your strengths, you'll lead in one of two areas: Learner and enterprise product. The experience of learning on Academy, and what companies need to bring to their teams: hands-on practice, assessment, credentials, reporting and integrations. Content systems. How content gets made and stays correct as fast as the product changes: authoring, preview, publishing and rollback for people who aren't engineers, Claude-assisted drafting with human review, reviewed versions for an industry or role, and checks that catch what's out of date. You may be a good fit if you Have 7+ years of software engineering experience, including products you owned from scoping through iteration in production Are strong across the stack, and can build both a polished front-end and the production services behind it Know the people you build for, whether they're learners, admins or authors, and can point to something you changed because of what you learned from them Have led technically complex, ambiguous work across teams, and can explain the architecture and its tradeoffs in depth Make the engineers around you better through review, design and example Have shipped LLM-powered features, or systems that depend on generated output, and can show how you knew the output was good Finish things, including the unglamorous last part Strong candidates may also have Built learning tools, taught, or written tutorials, courses or developer education Built authoring tools, a CMS, a docs platform or a publishing pipeline that non-engineers rely on Run experiments on activation, retention or learning outcomes, and can say what moved and why Built evals or automated quality checks for generated content Worked on assessment, credentials or enterprise administration features Worked on localization, structured content (such as MDX) or server rendering for content-heavy sites A strong design sense, and the habit of sweating the details of a user-facing surface The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work.
